title: packet-darwin: added decoding of the drop reason code
description:
On macOS, one can capture packets on the `droptap` interface to see packets that were dropped by the kernel.

The MR !19734 added the ability to dissect those packets, which includees dissecting the "drop reason code", e.g. `0x01010005`.

The Darwin kernel has code to map the above "drop reason code" bitmasks to human readable messages: https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/net/droptap.h

However, since the Darwin code is licensed under the APSL license, which isn't fully compatible with GPL, !19734 did not include the mapping.

For a disclosure, I am currently employed by Apple, and after many years of championing the benefits of Apple contributing back to Wireshark, I became the "Wireshark champion" in the company. Leveraging that role, I started a discussion with my partners in the Apple Legal department on how to expose the message mapping to Wireshark, while not exposing anyone to the (not fully clear) consequences of mixing APSL code with the GPL code. After weighing in all possible options, we have reached the conclusion that there is no way to contribute the APSL-licensed file to Wireshark, but we can create a separate file with the desired mapping (essentially a trimmed-down copy of he file [bsd/net/droptap.h](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/net/droptap.h)), licensed under _~~GPL-2.0~~_ _MIT_, and to contribute _that_ file to Wireshark. This split allows a complete separation of licenses and protects both Wireshark Foundation and Apple from any future liability due to a potential conflict between the APSL and GPL licenses.

_~~NOTE~~_~~ it is a hard requirement of Apple Legal department that the file will be licensed under the terms of _GPL-2.0-only_ and not _GPL-2.0-or-later_.~~

NOTE: due to a potential conflict of using _GPL-2.0-only_ in the Wireshark codebase, Apple Legal agreed to license the mapping under the terms of the _MIT_ license. 

This MR adds the trimmed down copy of the file that contains the mapping, licensed under _~~GPL-2.0-only~~_ _MIT_, as well as code in `epan/dissectors/packet-darwin.c` to make use of it.

Tested using the file `droptap.pcap` (attached)

Dissection result:

![Screenshot 2025-09-17 at 2.46.22 PM.png](/uploads/955ba0ae7642ce43a7047ea146502d00/Screenshot_2025-09-17_at_2.46.22_PM.png){width="2560" height="1440"}

[droptap.pcap](/uploads/9cb9669f6c9db6bd62b3374e6b9f2ec0/droptap.pcap)

* `packet-darwin.c`, which does not have any issues.

If needed, I can split the MR into two separate contributions: first the header file, then the C file.

Hi Omer, at first glance I don't think we can accept this as GPL-2.0-only since that would lock us into version 2.0 of the GPL. I'll check with the core development team to see if anyone can provide more insights.
Thanks @geraldcombs . I am checking with Legal if we can use MIT or BSD-3-clause instead.
@geraldcombs the Legal says that they support releasing this under the MIT license, but not under the BSD-3-Clause.
That's great news! Thanks for getting this sorted out.

commits_data.title: packet-darwin: added decoding of the drop reason code
commits_data.message:
packet-darwin: added decoding of the drop reason code

Adds the ability to decode the "drop reason code" into a human readable
description, as well as to filter by the "drop component" and "drop
domain".

The mapping of the "drop reason" to the human readable description is
contained in the header file
"epan/dissectors/packet-darwin-droptap-msg.h", which roughly follows the
structure of the file "bsd/net/droptap.h" in the source code of the
"xnu" kernel. This mapping was donated by Apple Inc. under the MIT
license.
